title: Style Over Substance: Evaluation Biases for Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the Elo ratings and win rates assigned by human annotators (crowd-sourced and experts) and LLM judges (GPT-4, Claude-1) for short (approx. 50 words) versus long (approx. 100 words) machine-generated answers.

Evaluating answer pairs in both forward and reversed directions to measure if human and LLM judges exhibit a disproportionate preference for the first (Assistant 1) or second (Assistant 2) answer presented.

Injecting deliberate grammatical mistakes (emulating intermediate/advanced English learners) versus factual errors into generated texts to observe if evaluators prioritize linguistic fluency and tone over factual substance.
